  The Solarium Project

  The Solarium Project is a grid-scale solar-battery pilot launched in 2019 in Nevada
  that
  pairs a photovoltaic array with 42 MWh of battery storage to smooth evening demand for
  the regional grid. The project is expanding significantly, with plans to increase
  total storage capacity to 90 MWh by 2027 and establish a second site in Arizona using
  shared control software and interconnect design.


  Current Operations

  The Nevada site has been operational since the project's founding in 2019. Its battery
  storage system—currently 42 MWh in capacity—enables the facility to address peak
  evening demand by storing solar energy generated during daylight hours. The project
  maintains transparency through quarterly performance summaries published on its
  official site. source http://127.0.0.1:8765/solarium_a.html


  Expansion Plans

  A major expansion is underway with storage capacity set to increase to 90 MWh by 2027.
  This growth will include a second operational site in Arizona, which will leverage the
  pilot program's proven control software and interconnect design rather than building
  from scratch. Permitting for the Arizona site is currently in progress, with
  construction milestones to be announced as the project advances. source
  http://127.0.0.1:8765/solarium_b.html
